PullRequest.Title: agentHost: retain client tools across nested session unsubscribe

## Summary

Fixes active-client lifecycle reconciliation when one nested session unsubscribes. The client now keeps its session-wide tool contribution while any active parent-session or sibling nested-session subscription remains across its live connections.

Explicit unsubscribe now follows the same session-level participation rule as reconnect. The active client and its orphaned calls are released only after the client has left the entire parent session. Existing nested-session tool routing, confirmation, and execution behavior remains unchanged.

Adds regressions for retention through parent, sibling, and nested-session subscriptions, plus cleanup after the last nested-session subscription is removed.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run hygiene` — passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --reporter dot` — 253 passing, 1 pending
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts` — passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path, nested iteration, per-subscription parsing, and one-notification-per-reference disposal are directly established in repository code. Exact user-visible duration depends on how many sessions/resources a client keeps live, so severity is low, but the scaling regression and critical-path reachability are not speculative.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous server-side iteration plus URI parsing/base64 decoding for every live subscription
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For S resident sessions and T remaining subscriptions, each unsubscribe now performs O(S*T) subscription checks; disposing T references emits T separate notifications, producing O(S*T^2) aggregate work (O(T^3) when held sessions scale with subscriptions).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased CPU and event-loop latency while closing or replacing many agent-session subscriptions
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An explicit unsubscribe released only the affected chat or iterated the affected parent session's chats, so disposing many references did not rescan unrelated sessions and subscriptions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every active state unsubscribe now invokes the reconnect-wide reconciliation. That method iterates all session URIs and calls _hasActiveSubscriptionToSession for each, which re-iterates all live connections/subscriptions and reparses chat URIs.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call `this._reconcileActiveClientSubscriptions(client)` at line 3084 replaces the deleted channel-local release logic; the changed reconciliation at lines 1203-1209 invokes the added nested subscription scan for every session.
Findings.Title: Avoid global reconciliation on every unsubscribe
Findings.Impact: Closing a window, session tree, or other owner with many held session/chat resources can monopolize the agent-host message loop before later protocol actions are processed. The trigger is a disposal burst across many open/retained agent sessions rather than a single ordinary unsubscribe.
Findings.Evidence: `AgentSubscriptionManager.dispose` and refcount release send one unsubscribe notification per resource, and `ProtocolServerHandler` handles each notification synchronously via `_removeSubscription`. `_reconcileActiveClientSubscriptions` scans `getSessionUris()`, while `_hasActiveSubscriptionToSession` scans every connection subscription and calls `parseChatUri`, which performs URI parsing and base64 decoding. Subscribed sessions are exempt from the default residency eviction, so S can grow with the set being disposed; there is no batching or coalescing between notifications.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep reconnect-wide reconciliation for reconnect/auth flows, but on explicit unsubscribe reconcile only the unsubscribed resource's owning session (after checking remaining parent/sibling subscriptions), or coalesce a disposal burst and precompute active parent-session URIs once so subscriptions are parsed once per pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose or explicitly unsubscribe session/chat subscriptions while another parent or sibling subscription remains
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The transport's synchronous onMessage handler calls _removeSubscription, agentService.unsubscribe, and then the newly added global _reconcileActiveClientSubscriptions before the message loop can process the next protocol message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Client sends an unsubscribe JSON-RPC notification over the existing protocol transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification per subscription whose final reference is disposed; a manager/window disposal can send T notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notifications existed, but each explicit unsubscribe performed channel-local cleanup rather than invoking reconnect-wide reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The notification itself is fire-and-forget, but each server handler runs the full synchronous reconciliation before subsequent messages are handled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number S of resident session states and number T of remaining state subscriptions across the client's live connections. AgentSubscriptionManager emits one notification per released resource, so a burst repeats the S-by-T scan for each resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unsubscribe notifications are handled serially on the agent-host event loop; there is no reconciliation coalescing, batching, limiter, or deferred pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session and subscription maps are warm in memory, but parent-session derivation is not cached: parseChatUri reparses and base64-decodes each subscription once per session per notification. Cold and warm behavior have the same iteration shape.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous call path, nested loops, per-subscription URI parsing, and per-reference notification behavior are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The default top-level residency limit is 10, but subscribed sessions are held resident and nested session state can increase the inventory. Exact latency depends on the number of concurrently held sessions/resources.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated-work regression because the diff puts a global nested scan on every unsubscribe and disposal bursts repeat it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unsubscribe the final nested/session subscription and release active-client tools and orphaned calls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After agentService.unsubscribe, reconciliation verifies no related active subscription, scans the session's chats for owned pending calls, then synchronously completes owned calls and removes the active client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast state action envelopes for newly completed orphaned tool calls and active-client removal to connected subscribers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one completion action per affected pending tool call plus one active-client removal action for the session; broadcasts fan out to currently subscribed clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A nested-chat unsubscribe released only that chat, so pending calls in sibling chats were not completed on this path; parent-session unsubscribe already iterated the session's chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Broadcast preparation and sends occur during synchronous cleanup before the unsubscribe handler returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in the affected session and pending client-owned tool calls; the global eligibility scan additionally scales with all resident sessions and subscriptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup is serialized in the unsubscribe message handler. State-action broadcasts occur synchronously through existing event dispatch; no parallel burst is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All state is memory-resident. No result cache or negative cache participates; each reconciliation rechecks chat and active-client state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added sibling-chat cleanup and broadcasts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously pending client-owned calls across sibling chats is typically small and no evidence shows a large realistic fanout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added per-chat cleanup is the required lifecycle behavior and scales with the calls that must be completed; the avoidable regression is the unrelated global rescan already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconnect restoration or relay-authentication expiry reconciles active-client participation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconnect waits for subscription restoration and then runs reconciliation before constructing replay/snapshot output. Authentication expiry releases connection subscriptions and runs reconciliation synchronously in its event callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect request/response and restored state-channel subscriptions over the protocol transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reconnect exchange per connection event, with subscriptions restored as the existing batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconnect already invoked reconciliation, but matching subscriptions were collected into a Set once rather than rescanned and reparsed for every session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changed reconciliation runs before replay or snapshot response construction, so its CPU cost is on reconnect latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential broadcasts for tool-call completion and active-client removal when restored subscriptions no longer retain a session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only sessions no longer represented by restored subscriptions; per affected pending call plus active-client removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old reconciliation already released unrepresented sessions and broadcast the corresponding actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during reconciliation before reconnect response progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resident sessions S, active subscriptions T, chats per session, and pending tool calls. The changed helper makes subscription matching O(S*T) instead of building a subscription set once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconnect subscription restoration is concurrent via its existing promise batch, but reconciliation itself is one synchronous pass after activation. Authentication-expiry handling is synchronous and serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Restored subscriptions are held in maps, but session ownership derived from chat URIs is recomputed for every session. There is no coalescing or memoization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the algorithmic change and reconnect critical-path placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect is less frequent than explicit unsubscribe bursts, and the default residency cap limits ordinary top-level-session cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported repeated-work mechanism also affects reconnect/auth expiry; no additional finding is needed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files. Reported one synchronous repeated-work regression caused by replacing channel-local unsubscribe cleanup with reconnect-wide reconciliation on every state unsubscribe. Traced retained-sibling, final-session cleanup, reconnect, and authentication-expiry paths; the broader final cleanup adds necessary action broadcasts but does not independently justify another performance finding.
